unmapped_findings: The yield strength of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al sample is not numerically resolved for the 500 °C/1 h condition in the text: Fig. 3(a) shows YS stays between roughly 350 and 450 MPa from 0Al to 4Al and then climbs steeply toward the 900 MPa gridline at 8Al, with the 450 °C/1 h curve dipping to its minimum at 6Al (block_id: figure_003, b0022, b0028).

Mass density at ~6 wt.% Al in the Fe-Mn-Al-C alloy series is about 7.15 g/cm³ (Fig. 1), with density falling from ~7.15 g/cm³ at 6 wt.% Al to ~6.4 g/cm³ at 13 wt.% Al; no specific printed density value is given for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al alloy itself (block_id: figure_001, b0011).

General κ-carbide description relevant to aged Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys: Al promotes the formation of nanoprecipitates upon aging with L′1₂ structure and approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)3AlC; these κ-carbides have an ordered fcc structure with lattice mismatch below 3% relative to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix and can form cuboidal nanoprecipitates. For the 6 wt.% Al intermediate variant, however, the aging-induced strengthening effect is reported as weak (block_id: b0015, b0024, b0025).
